subject: docs/coop/artifacts/product-boundary-preview.v1.json
subjectClass: PRODUCT-DISPOSITION-CANDIDATE, Route C, DR-010 / DR-117 / DR-011-R16, preview only
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. Every attack axis fails. The load-bearing test is the seven-item enumeration, because this candidate's whole claim is that it dispositions file 02's seven binding product-boundary items without changing them — and PB-1 through PB-7 map to file 02's seven successor items in exact order by string equality, with the three V1 decisions (P-1, P-2, G3) correctly excluded from that count. The two claims most likely to be overreach are both refused in the document's own text: enforcement evidence is disclaimed in three separate places as non-admission rather than qualification, and D-002's TypeScript role is expressly characterised as a slice role selection rather than a G3 successor, which the packet's own G3 definition — a Rust host/core with bundled TypeScript provider and pinned rustc_driver sidecar — confirms it is not. All four cited digests match live bytes. I tested two candidate advisories and both resolved in the document's favour, so I am returning zero rather than manufacturing findings.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 060220c07fe4ab78e04b55dd0f895de0f1d5d2af69c9a09ea254d1af8cf2896d, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at c1fdd0e1b93aba1bd0c882bc3d80e9703328ce1c54c5afd68a1a48dbf0e46cec, also read-only.

The attack 'changes file 02's seven-item count' fails, and I tested the mapping rather than the count. Under the pinned heading '## Current V1 product boundary and required successors', file 02 enumerates ten bullets: the first three are the V1 decisions P-1, P-2 and G3, and the remaining seven are the required-successor items. PB-1 through PB-7 correspond to those seven in exact order, matching by string equality after punctuation normalisation — marketplace/catalog and governance depth; external lifecycle parity and discovery; contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only; untrusted native or WASM admission and required enforcement evidence; imperative contributions, probes, project hooks, and root commands; network-granted analysis and egress defaults; replacement of the full-default G3 physical substrate. The candidate neither adds, drops, reorders nor rewords an item, and whatThisDoesNotDo states 'Does not change file 02's seven-item enumeration.'

The seven-item pin's authority is real. D-011 is titled 'Register content: DR-117 widened to file 02's seven binding items (V2TOPIC-F-04)' and is ADOPTED, and file 08's DR-117 row reads 'Product-boundary successor covering the SEVEN binding product-boundary items enumerated at file 02 §product boundary'. The candidate's note — 'D-011: DR-117 covers these seven by reference. Any change to that enumeration re-opens DR-117' — is accurate, and its remeasurementClause carries the consequence: if the enumeration changes, DR-117 re-opens and the candidate cannot be recorded against the new enumeration.

The attack 'claims QUALIFIED enforcement evidence' fails in three independent places. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled lists 'Enforcement evidence as QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED. Exclusion by non-admission is the preview posture, not a demonstrated confinement proof.' whatThisDoesNotDo states 'Does not claim QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED.' And enforcementHonesty names the gap against its own acceptance criterion rather than hiding it: 'File 08's DR-010 acceptance cell asks for trust and enforcement evidence. This candidate supplies a product posture of non-admission, not a qualified enforcement harness.' I checked that cell — it reads 'Explicit product-owner successor covering catalog/lifecycle depth, contribution ontology, default substrate/profile, trust and enforcement evidence' — so the disclaimer is against the correct text, and the four gates it routes qualification to (DR-G07, DR-G09, DR-G21, DR-128) all exist in the corpus.

The attacks 'replaces G3' and 'treats D-002 TypeScript role as a G3 successor' fail, and the packet's own definition is what settles it. The product packet records G3-SUBSTRATE as status CONFIRMED, choice DELIVERY_V2_BINDING, rule 'Rust host/core, bundled TypeScript provider, bundled exactly pinned rustc_driver sidecar, full default install profile, finite supported-platform matrix, and offline assets are the v1 substrate defaults.' D-002's preview is a TypeScript-only, CLI-first analysis slice, which is plainly not that. PB-7 says so — 'That is a slice role selection, not a G3 successor. G3 remains the V1 substrate default. Preview does not ship a new default substrate/profile' — and whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not amend P-1, P-2, G3-SUBSTRATE, or CD-RT-5 in the product packet.'

The P-1 and P-2 recitals are faithful to the packet. Every substantive token of the candidate's P-1 text ('NO_ECOSYSTEM_DEPTH_FOR_V1. No marketplace, public lifecycle parity, extension discovery service, or ecosystem governance depth.') and P-2 text ('NARROW_CONTRIBUTION_ONTOLOGY. Contributions are narrow producers or data-only rules/profiles. They never own root commands, policy, persistence, rendering, termination, or host lifecycle.') appears in the packet's choice and rule fields for those decisions. The G3 recital's only extra tokens are the candidate's own commentary sentence, not a misquotation.

The attacks 'opens a marketplace or admits untrusted code' fail. PB-1 excludes marketplace, public catalog and governance depth; PB-2 excludes external lifecycle parity and discovery, admitting 'First-party/explicitly-trusted install only'; PB-3 admits 'only first-party/explicitly-trusted components under DR-128's MVP boundary'; PB-4 states untrusted native and WASM 'are not admitted' with DR-128 remaining post-MVP. Each tracks D-002, which records 'DR-128 excludes third-party/untrusted scope from MVP', 'Components: first-party/explicitly-trusted only (DR-128's MVP boundary)' and 'DR-128 (post-MVP by register)'. The DR-116 deferral the candidate cites is also real — D-002 lists 'DR-116 (no third-party support policy needed yet)'.

PB-5 and PB-6 check out against their cited sources. D-002 describes doctor as 'read-only/no-network default, consented probes', which is what PB-6 asserts, and PB-5's characterisation of consented probes as host acts under D-032 / doctor-contract.v4 rather than contribution-granted probes is consistent with those adopted decisions.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails on every surface: status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, whatThisDoesNotDo opening with 'Does not mark DR-010, DR-117, or DR-011-R16 SATISFIED', and condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded closing with 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording.' That last clause forecloses my own verdict being read as the recording.

The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses it, and condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded preserves 'Conditions 2-5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/.'

The authority claim is exact, which I checked because it is the kind of clause that overreaches quietly. D-000's decision text reads 'The assistant completes the coop design end-to-end, making coordinator/product-authority decisions on the user's behalf', and file 08's DR-010 owner cell is 'Product owner'. So a product-authority draft for this row is squarely inside D-000's delegation — unlike the V1 owner-role recordings, which run on D-054's separate and narrower grant. The candidate does not confuse the two, and it still requires independent review and disclaims being the recording.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails. All four verify: COORD d0284aab…, file 08 6547e6ac…, file 02 1811c682…, and the product packet bbe24527…. The packet digest is also the exact value file 08's DR-010 evidence cell pins, and the candidate's three selectors correspond to that cell's '$.decisions.{P-1,P-2,G3-SUBSTRATE}'.
The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: file 08 matches its cited digest and git reports zero modified tracked files. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

Examined as a possible advisory and cleared: the annotation 'DR-117 (condition 2)'. I checked whether DR-117 really sits under condition 2 rather than being condition 2. Condition 2 is 'all 29 rows classified', and its text explicitly lists DR-117 among the route-C PREFERENCE-LADEN product decisions, alongside DR-104, DR-115, DR-116, DR-118, DR-119, DR-123, DR-128 and DR-129. The annotation is accurate and apt, since this candidate is itself a route-C product disposition.

Examined as a possible advisory and cleared: PB-7's phrase 'D-002 selected TypeScript as the sole preview language role'. The word 'sole' does not appear in D-002, but D-002 selects a single TypeScript slice and refers to 'this one role' when scoping DR-118's outstanding work, so the characterisation is accurate rather than an embellishment.

The candidate is conservative about its own reach in a way I tested rather than assumed: it names three register rows but claims condition-1 effect for DR-010 only, holding that 'DR-117 (condition 2) and DR-011-R16 remain independently required; a later recording may close them only within the same preview exclusion scope, never by claiming a full P-1/P-2/G3 successor.'
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Whether the product owner, as a human, would record this disposition. This is a candidate drafted under D-000's product-authority delegation, and it states that its own existence is not the recording. The recording act is a separate step outside this review.

Whether excluding all seven items is the right product choice. This is a PREFERENCE-LADEN Route C decision; I tested that the exclusions are honestly stated, correctly scoped to the preview, and consistent with the V1 decisions they claim to preserve — not whether a different product posture would be better.

The substance of DR-G07, DR-G09, DR-G21 and DR-128 as qualification gates. I confirmed each exists in the corpus and that qualification is routed to them rather than claimed here; I did not audit what those gates require.
The internal contents of the product packet beyond the three pinned selectors P-1, P-2 and G3-SUBSTRATE, plus confirming CD-RT-5 exists and is untouched by this candidate.

Whether file 02's seven-item enumeration is itself the right enumeration. I verified the candidate reproduces it exactly and re-opens DR-117 if it changes; the enumeration's own merits belong to D-011, which adopted it.
DR-011-R16's specific content. The candidate leaves it independently required, which is the conservative disposition, but I did not audit that residual.

acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. The thing that could most easily have gone wrong here is substituting a convenient seven for file 02's seven, and it does not happen — the mapping is exact and in order, with the three V1 decisions correctly kept out of the count. The document is also honest exactly where honesty costs it something: it concedes that file 08's DR-010 cell asks for trust and enforcement evidence and that non-admission is not that, rather than dressing exclusion up as confinement. I record explicitly that I went looking for advisories in the two places the drafting is loosest — the 'sole preview language role' phrasing and the 'DR-117 (condition 2)' annotation — and both survived checking, so I am reporting none rather than padding the verdict.
